top_story.headline: Quiet Saturday: no disclosures, FARA filings or top-official contacts; lobbying amendments dominate
top_story.dek: The only new material today is 62 lobbying filings, led by a former National Security Council aide's defense-industry client list and a string of amended Lyft reports.
paragraphs: No House or Senate financial disclosures, no FARA filings and no filings naming the President, Vice President or a cabinet official were reported in this window. The Office of Government Ethics reported no new filings, and the deterministic extras (deadlines, ethics agreements, presidential trades, pardon lobbying, stopped traders) found nothing.

In lobbying, the most notable pattern is Aubrey Maturin LLC, whose third-quarter reports list Adrielle Churchill Wiese, a former National Security Council senior director for legislative affairs, as a covered former official lobbying for eight defense and manufacturing clients, including Thales Defense & Security, Inc. (report).
Separately, Lyft filed amended reports for all four quarters of a prior year span, with amounts ranging from $170,000 to $480,000 in expenses across the filings listed below.

sections.headline: No New Office of Government Ethics Filings Reported Today
paragraphs: The U.S. Office of Government Ethics website reported no new ethics filings or divestitures within the current window. Routine monitoring will resume with the next data release.

sections.headline: No new House or Senate disclosures in this window
paragraphs: The input lists zero House and zero Senate filings since October 28 that earlier editions had not already reported. The Senate eFD check also failed with a parsing error (see footer), so Senate coverage for this window is incomplete.

blocks.text: No House or Senate filings were available to report. The Senate eFD fetch returned an error, so the absence of Senate filings is not confirmed.

sections.headline: No new registrations; seven terminations and a heavy load of amendments
paragraphs: Of 62 LDA filings posted since October 30, there were 36 third-quarter reports, 5 third-quarter no-activity reports, and a large number of amendments. No new registrations appeared. Seven terminations were filed, five of them no-activity terminations or termination amendments from Pyxis Partners, LLC. The table below covers the terminations and the activity reports with a signal; the remaining 27 filings with no signal (20 of the 55 activity reports plus 7 others counted in the totals) are not detailed, and the 15 Criscom and Lyft items are grouped where similar.

items: Lyft filed amended reports across quarters, each lobbying on ridesharing, veterans' non-emergency medical transportation and related issues: see CSL entry above for the largest amended report in the batch. Lyft amendments: $330,000 (Q4), $330,000 (Q2, covered positions Allison Cullin and Courtney Temple), $330,000 (Q1), $330,000 (Q3, includes algorithmic pricing), $260,000 (Q3), $260,000 (Q4), $230,000 (Q1), $170,000 (Q2).

The Criscom Company filed third-quarter reports for local-government clients, all on budget and appropriations, with covered positions Charles Jelloian and Reuben Shortnacy: Hidden Villa Ranch, City of Sanger, Mariposa County Sheriff's Office, Imperial County Sheriff's Office, City of Avenal, Kings County Sheriff's Office, City of Holtville, North Fork Community Power, City of Wasco (Q3) and City of Wasco (Q2).

Council of the Great City Schools (report) lobbied on the FY2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations bill and several special-education bills; National Association of State Directors of Career Technical Education (report) lobbied on Perkins Act implementation and Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act reauthorization.
